author: Codex critical design seat /root/design91_option_rule
task: Finite decision only: assess round04 L-W against legal cancellable low-priority prepare + one ordinary partial-translation cache + late allocation. Do not duplicate root L-M.

conclusion.decision: Pause advancement of the separate L-W PTE-saving/performance-algorithm claim this round. The positive root/middle/leafY hand example is reproducible by a concrete fixed-request control. Complete area, restart latency and frequency differences are unknown, so no independent cheaper/faster L-W architecture is established.
conclusion.new_critical_fact: Y in L-W's3-PTE example is a cold leaf. An actual fixed-Y WRITE translation miss is itself a higher-priority demand and can interrupt optional prepareX under US9542332B2, even without a competing A request. A set-specific cross-address cancellation witness is not necessary for this case.
conclusion.cache_term_correction: One physically indexed cached PTE cannot freely skip both consumed prefix levels. The one-entry strong control is a standard virtual-prefix-indexed partial-translation cache: prefix/context -> next leaf-table PPN. This precise cache organization is covered by Barr ISCA2010. It can skip both prefix reads with one entry; its complete tag/output/invalidation state must be paid.
conclusion.proof_boundary: Concrete control equality of useful PTE accesses is a new bounded judgment about this L-W hand example. It is not proof that every complete implementation cost is equal, that an exact SET-WRITE integration was published, or that the whole research field has no open problem.
conclusion.publishability: Because the complete simple control reproduces the avoided unchosen leaf, that PTE saving cannot establish an independent algorithm contribution. If a precisely costed goal-continuation implementation offers an actual area/latency frontier the control cannot match, and nearest work does not cover that integration, a specialized architecture could still contribute. No such full-cost evidence exists in this round.

candidate_scope.conditions: Pinned single-stage nonglobal4KiB mappings; all accepted output slots in one2MiB virtual subtree, exact same registered context/root epoch. Real64B COPY and normal source READ. A newly FREE accepted Y appears after root/middle processing but before any leaf AR firstVALID.
candidate_scope.promised_action: Choose Y within the already checked common prefix, read/check leafY, then generate/translate a stable actual chosen WRITE and perform all AW/W/B.
candidate_scope.ordinary_address_boundary: No existing fixed-X DMA parent or concrete upstream AW is rewritten. The candidate needs a new set-valued immutable pool parent. The control can use the same ordinary late-allocation parent semantics while its actual IOMMU/PTW requests are individually fixed.

complete_control.name: Fixed optional prefix preparation + one-entry virtual-prefix translation cache + ordinary late fixed-Y WRITE
raw_start: Use identical original COPY descriptors/arrival times, accepted-slot constraints, pool mapping/setup, consumer ownership/cache-sync/release and native resources. All actual normal source READs, permissions, payload retention, completion and CPU/MMIO work are charged.

Do not inject a warm PWC or force the control to inherit the candidate's completed prefix. The PWC becomes valid only after this control itself legally reads/validates the actual root and middle PTEs, or after the same charged real history supplies it.

Allow the control to prepare earlier, select early, wait for a hot slot, use an efficient successful-prepare continuation and all actual eight AX heads/native data buffering. No one-child or extra-walker fiction.
The ordinary allocator observes the same paid exact ownership/class/accepted-set information. The control does not learn future release events or borrow Y permissions from X.
complete_control.immutable_parent: Latch src,pool,accepted_mask,length,tag,context/options and epoch in the ordinary pool/late-allocation frontend. Parent VALID and accepted fields remain stable. No concrete output address has been publicly promised before allocation.

prepareX.request: Choose a representative legal X inside the registered subtree. Issue a fixed, optional nonarchitectural PREPARE(X,WRITE-context,ticket,epoch), rather than a concrete X AXI AW. X and its access/context fields remain fixed for that prepare's lifetime.
prepareX.permissions: Normal device/context checks govern the preparation. Every non-leaf consumed uses the normal validity/reserved/stage/error processing; no leaf permissions are inferred from the prefix. Optional preparation faults do not become a false successful COPY.
prepareX.memory: The PTW emits ordinary root and middle PTE reads. Each AR is stable from firstVALID, including while !READY. After accepted AR, its R must be consumed even if the prepare is cancelled.
prepareX.checkpoint: For an unbound output operation whose registered accepted set is wholly within this common2MiB subtree, the wrapper has a bounded prefix checkpoint. At middle response, store the validated partial translation and request generic stop before any leaf AR is first offered. This fixed checkpoint does not need to predict which Y will later release. If control chooses full preparation instead, its actual extra leaf/reuse costs are counted.
prepareX.timing_cost: Stopping at the checkpoint, publishing a cache entry and issuing a new fixed request are paid state transitions. They may add cycles. They are not free software round trips or assumed zero-cycle hardware. L-W also pays its own ownership/leaf selection and new interface timing.

partial_cache.meaning: One virtual-prefix translation-cache entry stores the combined partial mapping from the common upper VPN indices and exact context/root epoch to the leaf-table physical base. It is not a cache entry holding one arbitrary physical PTE, and not a free alias for all root/middle entries.
partial_cache.fill: Only a checked middle response can install the combined result. A malformed prefix cannot fill it. Capture relevant accumulated non-leaf state, such as global status; initial nonglobal scope may conservatively reject all global ancestors.
partial_cache.key: Full relevant virtual prefix, source device/context policy identity, PSCID,GSCID,enabled stages and a root/mapping epoch/invalidation contract. No cross-context mapping inference from equal physical pages.
partial_cache.invalidation: Normal translation invalidation/reconfiguration wins over cache fill/use. A matching invalidate clears it; uncertain association uses conservative whole-entry clear. Prefix validity cannot outlive its mapping contract.
partial_cache.retention: A one-entry implementation can pin the checkpoint only until the fixed chosen-Y request consumes it, with bounded hold and a pin bit. A real competing demand still proceeds; it may bypass PWC insertion while pinned. Retention interference is priced. If the entry is evicted or invalidated, the control rereads normally; compare equivalent retention/fault conditions for L-W.
partial_cache.native_status: The present native PTW has neither this PWC nor generic ticketed cancel. These are modifications for a strong allowed control, not falsely claimed existing native features.

cancellation_and_ownership: Optional X-prepare terminates with CANCELLED(ticket,epoch), distinct from COPY completion/error. Poison its return route and do not generate X WRITE from any late result.
If any next AR has already become firstVALID, retain/drain it; only subsequent unpublished ARs can be suppressed. A cancel edge cannot retract VALID&&!READY.

The higher-priority actual Y miss can provide the ordinary cancellation trigger if it arrives early enough. Otherwise the bounded prefix checkpoint prevents premature X leaf publication while ownership/selection is being resolved. Do not assume the allocator+normal-miss lookup fits magically before the next AR.

Ordinary late allocation atomically reserves a genuinely FREE, accepted Y. Existing actual leases remain exclusive, generation/cache synchronization is validated, and outputs with different contexts/permissions are not interchangeable by declaration.

After choosing Y, issue a new normal fixed-Y WRITE translation request. This request's fields remain stable from firstVALID. The cancelled X request and new Y request have separate ticket/owner identities; no in-flight request is silently reassigned.
finish: On the actual Y IOTLB miss, lookup the one-entry virtual-prefix cache. An exact match loads the validated leaf-table base and the Y leaf index; no root/middle memory reread is required.

Compute and freeze leafY's physical PTE AR address before its firstVALID. Read/check the actual leafY, including permissions/privilege/stage/A-D/error handling, and install/return according to the normal selected-translation path.

The actual normal immutable WRITE performs its remaining standard permission/relookup/physical-header acceptance path exactly as charged for L-W; no PA voucher or grant reuse is free. Allow a priced legitimate continuation for either side.
Execute all actual AW/W beats and final B; report the actual chosen output only after normal COPY completion and cache synchronization. Reserved completion space cannot trap issued responses.
pseudocode: admit ordinary late-allocation COPY parent from raw original trace; latch stable set/context; execute normal source READ and retain its real data
optional PREPARE_X: fixed X/context/ticket; read/check root; read/check middle
at configured unbound-prefix checkpoint: publish checked PREFIX_CACHE entry, stop optional X before next AR publication, return CANCELLED_X; drain any already-published AR first
ordinary allocator: on real ownership state choose FREE accepted Y and atomically reserve it; create stable normal WRITE_Y child
on actual WRITE_Y miss: ordinary demand priority may terminate optional X if still active; after legal cancel acknowledgment, normal Y owns the walker
PWC exact hit: set next table base; issue stable leafY AR; normal leaf checks/fill/reply
normal actual WRITE_Y: same permissions/translation handoff, W/B and completion as candidate
on invalidation/error/no matching prefix: normal restart/fault/bounded fallback; never reuse stale prefix/grants

hand_equivalence.initial_case: X and Y share validated root+middle indices; Y becomes a legal FREE output before an unpublished leaf. The chosen output is Y for both implementations.
hand_equivalence.numeric: For an assumed10-unit PTE service, both L-W and the concrete control pay30 units of PTE service. The old complete-X control pays40. The supposed10-unit saving is already reproducible; normal data/permissions/consumer costs are common but still charged.
hand_equivalence.actual_COPY_cost: The one64B COPY still needs a real source endpoint check/AR/R8, a chosen WRITE endpoint check/AW/W8/B, descriptor/ownership and completion. Stopping a preparation does not remove payload transfer, replace a permission check or create another walker.
hand_equivalence.latency_formula: C_LW=C_common+30+delta_LW; C_control=C_common+30+delta_checkpoint+delta_cancel/reissue+delta_PWC (minus any legal overlap). C_common is not fixed across original-start policies by fiat. Native deltas, port conflicts, area and Fmax are not established.
exact_boundaries: If Y's normal demand reaches arbitration before X leaf firstVALID, published demand-priority preemption supplies the cancel action directly.

If Y lookup/selection arrives later, the control must pay a bounded prefix hold/checkpoint. Without that hold an already-published leafX must drain and may add one PTE. L-W's own selection stage and firstVALID timing must be equally priced.

If both implementations hold at the same correct checkpoint, their required PTE sequence is identical. A difference in internal single-walk versus cancelled/restarted request identity is not by itself a new useful system capability.
If X's completed leaf is later useful, the complete-X preparation may provide a genuine future hit. Both candidate and control must include that reuse, not count leafX as automatically waste.

full_cost_status.example_PWC_fields: An illustrative conservative one-entry field subset using native VPN29/PPN44: prefix20+PSCID20+GSCID16+stage2+epoch32+SID24+next_table_PPN44+global1+valid1+pin1+level2 =163 bits,ceil21B. This assumes the normal context/invalidation contract described above and is not a complete cost claim.
full_cost_status.correction: Omitting SID may be legal if the surrounding checked context contract proves it unnecessary; reduce both designs consistently. Trimming high VPN bits or tying level/stage constants applies to both. Root/root-PPN binding must be covered by epoch/invalidation or explicitly stored; cannot silently drop it.
additionally_price: Cache tag comparator/output mux, epoch and invalidate routing, one-entry fill/consume/pin arbitration, and any PWC pipeline/skid.
Prepare fixed-request command, owner/ticket/terminal return, optional-fault handling, stable-AR drain/cancel implementation and the checkpoint control.
Ordinary actual normal Y request buffering, permission/data response ownership, job continuation/callback, selected-slot report and fault/error draining.
L-W's immutable set-goal metadata, allowed-mask/ownership read/selector, continuation association and live prefix lifetime, its own stable AR output/pipelines and normal-result routing.
Shared ordinary parent/payload/pool/kernel generation/consumer cache-sync/native in-flight resources; avoid duplicating them on only the control.
Legal recycling of dead X-prepare fields and overlap of cancellation acknowledgment/cache lookup with new request stages; cannot artificially force every control field to remain live forever.
Same-budget ordinary cache/concurrency/layout; powers-of-two/native masks, Fmax and buffer backpressure, rather than byte arithmetic alone.
full_cost_status.decision: The163-bit entry example is a subset, not proof control is more expensive by163bits. L-W may remove that entry but add goal/selector state and timing; control may recycle or simplify fields. No full two-layout ledger or hardware evidence establishes a useful area/latency frontier.
full_cost_status.speculative_difference_only: Keeping a private live prefix might avoid ordinary reissue/PWC lookup and persistent-cache metadata. This is a concrete engineering hypothesis, not a verified advantage and not an independent PTE-saving rule.

primary_source_review.title: Translation Caching: Skip, Don't Walk (the Page Table)
primary_source_review.direct_scope: This finite review newly opened the author12-page PDF and directly read §3.2/3.3 and §4.1, PDFpp3-4, retrieved lines296-371,393-410.
primary_source_review.supports: Virtual-prefix-indexed partial-translation entries let a later address skip multiple upper radix levels. A single translation/path entry differs from a physically indexed single PTE. Prefix reuse and its ordinary cache implementation are old.
primary_source_review.does_not_establish: The paper is not an exact COPY_TO_SET/lifetime API. It does not prove every L-W integration cost equals this control.

primary_source_review.title: System and method for performing hardware prefetch tablewalks having lowest tablewalk priority
primary_source_review.direct_scope: Previously read in round04; this turn re-opened exact FIG3/4 design lines451-476 to check the normal-Y-demand trigger.
primary_source_review.supports: Higher-priority new demand terminates low-priority prefetch outside noninterruptible regions. FLUSH and CANCEL controls are explicit; actual architectural modification/fault situations are restricted.
primary_source_review.does_not_establish: The disclosure is not proof the current RISC-V/AXI RTL already supports cancel. Its integration here must preserve published ARs. It does not supply an arbitrary zero-cost bitmap allocator or guarantee a safe cancel point after every desired event.

primary_source_review.title: Processor to detect redundancy of page table walk
primary_source_review.direct_scope: Previously read in round04; this turn re-opened lines337-403, especially383-400.
primary_source_review.supports: An ongoing redundant walk can stop; checked common-prefix translations are cached; replay then skips prefix levels. Cancel+cached-prefix reuse is concretely disclosed, not invented solely to reject L-W.
primary_source_review.does_not_establish: Its exact example concerns redundant shared page-table work, not the presented DMA output-set semantics. Do not equate patent coverage with a legal patent opinion or published exact new-contract coverage.

remaining_route.user_pause_boundary: This finite review yields no new independent L-W benefit beyond the explicit reproduction boundary. Do not start another model/RTL/build or broad mechanism direction merely to continue activity.
remaining_route.shortest_positive_redesign: Only if resumed with a specific cost hypothesis, recast L-W as a bounded implementation question: can a live private prefix continuation eliminate enough legitimate cancel/reissue/PWC state or cycles under the same immutable-parent and permission contracts to improve a complete area/latency frontier? First write the two minimal complete state/port/control ledgers. A full legal control with equal/lower cost ends this route; an actual unavoidable cost difference is the required new fact. This round did not execute that work.
remaining_route.not_a_field_exhaustion_claim: The hand example being reproducible rules out using that example as an independent algorithm proof. It does not say that the entire IOMMU/DMA field or every endpoint-choice mechanism has been studied exhaustively.
remaining_route.no_unbounded_followup: Keep possible later evaluation limited to the specified common-prefix/firstVALID/owner-cost comparison; do not produce additional speculative directions in this round.
